newsitem.title: UK: Work crowds out many young Britons' home life.
newsitem.headline: Work crowds out many young Britons' home life.

text.p: One in five young Britons are so pressured at work that they would be willing to take a pay cut to gain more time with their families or hobbies, a survey reported on Monday.
It showed that many younger people, both single and married, are increasingly concerned about the lack of balance between their work and homelife.
One quarter of male employees under 45 felt that family life and career progress were not compatible.
High earners were particularly affected, the survey of 2,000 adults carried out by MORI showed.
Of 50 percent who worried about having too little home life, concern was greatest among managers and those who work in large companies and the professions.
The survey was conducted for WFD, an American consultancy which helps businesses understand the impact of the work/life balance on their operations.
